topology: R1/R2/R3 AS65000 form full-mesh iBGP using OSPF-reachable Loopback0 peers 10.255.1.1/2.2/3.3. R3 peers with R4 AS65100 over 172.16.34.0/30. R1 originates the client LAN 192.168.10.0/24; R4 originates service LAN 192.168.40.0/24. PC1 and SRV1 exercise all four routers; PC2/R2 are independent local controls. R3 Loopback10 10.254.3.3/32 is prepared for next-hop-only withdrawal.
implemented: Thirtieth ENARSI lab with independent practice/reference attempts, seven-row plan, ordinary IOS/Windows verification and current-domain/path/query permalinks. Sixteen tasks preserve the existing UI, themes, icons, terminal and single-file offline use.

Initial eight directed peer views are Established. R1/R2 retain received service paths with inaccessible external next hop 172.16.34.2; those paths have no valid/best state, RIB installation or re-advertisement. Actual failed service probes and working independent controls earn diagnosis.

R3 next-hop-self toward both internal peers repairs resolution through OSPF Loopback0. R1/R2 install iBGP AD200, next hop10.255.3.3 and AS path65100; R3 installs eBGP AD20. Reverse client routes retain internal AS semantics, and R4 receives path65000. CEF and actual traffic follow physical transit.

Six exercises cover missing next-hop-self, bad outbound next-hop policy, bad local inbound policy, working recursively resolved static /32 next-hop routes, next-hop-only OSPF withdrawal/recovery, and working passive external-transit OSPF reachability. Each requires observed traffic followed by fresh baseline restoration.

Outbound NH-OUT changes only R1 advertisements; NH-IN changes only local R1 import while R3 advertised-routes remain correct. R2 retains the correct path. Both incidents require actual failed service requests and working independent controls before repair credit.

Static resolution adds only 172.16.34.2/32 via OSPF-reachable R3 Lo0 on R1/R2, preserving the BGP next-hop attribute. IGP resolution passively originates the external /30 without making R4 an OSPF peer or redistributing host LANs. Both alternatives require complete HTTP before cleanup and fresh restored baseline traffic.

NH-RECURSE advertises 10.254.3.3 while all peers use Lo0. Prove alternate forwarding/HTTP, withdraw only Lo10 OSPF membership, observe retained inaccessible paths while all eight channel IDs remain Established, restore alternate forwarding/HTTP, then remove the policy and temporary IGP scope and prove baseline restoration.

Seven live and nine observed checks: practice0, diagnosis1, baseline10, full16, completed reference only seven live. Three unique ICMP requests per direction correlate actual destination acceptance, physical router egress and parent-linked replies. Failed requests need real No route drops; HTTP needs reassembled TCP response data. YAML preserves earned observations and rebuilds live protocol state.
Existing route-map set help/Tab grammar now exposes implemented ip next-hop syntax and validates its arguments. No networking-engine change was required.
scope: IOS IPv4 unicast BGP next-hop reachability using full-mesh iBGP, a directly connected eBGP peer, recursive static/OSPF resolution and import/export next-hop policy. Cisco primary documentation reviewed; no fresh CML capture or complete binary BGP interoperability is claimed. No UI or terminal-theme changes.
